overview: Two 1938 records: a cross-reference on journalist Kinjiro Watanabe denying espionage claims in Mexico City, and a memo on Domei's new Hong Kong office, which failed to gain Chinese subscribers despite soliciting over twenty papers, suspected of propaganda purposes.

people.name: Kinjiro Watanabe
people.role: Japanese newspaperman resident in Mexico City

people.name: Robert Y. Horiguchi
people.role: American-trained newspaperman placed in charge of the Domei News Agency office in Hong Kong

people.name: Addison E. Southard
people.role: U.S. Consul General in Hong Kong

people.name: Ringwalt
people.role: Division of Far Eastern Affairs staff member identified in the drafting notation

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Military Attaché report on Kinjiro Watanabe
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to a report on Japanese newspaperman Kinjiro Watanabe’s response to allegations of Japanese espionage in the Central American press.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a report on Kinjiro Watanabe, a Mexico City newspaperman who denied espionage charges from a KEN article.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Domei News Agency office in Hong Kong
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes a Hong Kong telegram concerning the establishment, clientele, and suspected propaganda purpose of Domei’s new local office.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Domei opened a Hong Kong office under Horiguchi, suspected of pure propaganda purpose; it failed to gain any of twenty-plus solicited Chinese subscribers, only three other clients.

interest: Shows Japanese press/propaganda monitoring in Mexico and Hong Kong, including a failed Domei bid for Chinese subscribers.
